Comic Scraper

Comic Zone User Guide — finding, verifying, and applying comic metadata with ComicVine.

1. What Comic Scraper Does

Comic Scraper is Comic Zone's built-in metadata tool. It searches ComicVine for the comic or collected edition you selected, ranks likely matches, lets you verify ambiguous results, and applies available information to your library.

Depending on the information available, scraping can update series, title, issue or volume number, year, publisher, release information, descriptions, story arcs, characters, teams, locations, creators, cover artwork, and other issue information.

Not every ComicVine entry contains the same fields, so the amount of metadata available varies by comic.

2. Before You Scrape

Matching works best when Comic Zone has a recognizable series, issue or volume number, and year. Clean filenames can provide these values even when existing metadata is limited.

For example, Avengers 031 (2025).cbz gives Comic Zone a likely series of Avengers, issue 31, and year 2025. Collected editions may use indicators such as Vol., Volume, Book, TPB, HC, Deluxe, or a v-number.

3. Starting Comic Scraper

Select one or more comics and start Comic Scraper. Comic Zone first shows a confirmation window telling you how many selected comics will be processed.

Start Scraping

Begins processing the selected comic or comics.

Configure

Opens the scraper configuration options so you can adjust the scrape before it starts.

Cancel

Closes the confirmation window without starting the scrape.

4. Cover Preview and Scraping Progress

After scraping begins, the Cover Preview identifies the comic currently being processed and shows its existing cover. This is especially helpful during a multi-comic scrape.

Left to scrape shows how many items remain. Cancel stops the active scraping operation.

5. ComicVine Results

When Comic Zone needs help choosing between possible matches, the ComicVine Results window appears. The search description at the top shows what Comic Zone is attempting to identify.

The table includes Title, Year, Issues, and Publisher. Selecting a row updates the cover preview. Comic Zone ranks results so a strong candidate normally appears near the top, but ambiguous titles should still be verified.

6. Result Window Controls

Apply

Applies the selected ComicVine result and stores the available metadata with the comic.

Skip

Leaves the current comic unchanged and continues. Use this when no displayed result is correct or you want to identify the comic later.

Search Again

Runs another search. This is useful when extra filename text, an incorrect year, or an unusual title produces poor matches.

Show Issues

Opens the selected ComicVine volume so you can inspect the entries inside it before applying the match.

Close

Closes the ComicVine Results window.

7. Verifying a Volume with Show Issues

Use Show Issues when several results look plausible or when you want to confirm that the requested issue or collected volume exists inside the selected ComicVine volume.

The list displays available titles and numbers. Selecting an entry updates the cover preview, letting you compare its title, number, and artwork before applying the match.

8. Single Issues and Collected Editions

Comic Scraper is not limited to traditional numbered issues. Comic Zone can also work with collected editions when the filename contains recognizable volume information.

  • Batman 162 (2026)
  • Action Comics 1080 (2025)
  • Avengers by Jed MacKay v06 (2026) - The Grail
For collected editions, compare the volume title, number, year, publisher, cover, and Show Issues entries rather than relying on the series name alone.

9. Scraping Multiple Comics

Select multiple comics before starting Comic Scraper to process them as a queue. Comic Zone advances through the selection and asks for input when necessary. After Apply or Skip, it can prepare the next comic while nonessential metadata work continues in the background.

Watch the Cover Preview during a large batch. The comic name, cover, and remaining count help confirm that the results correspond to the comic currently being processed.

10. How Matching Works

Comic Zone evaluates several clues when ranking ComicVine results, including series-name similarity, issue or volume number, expected year, publisher, whether the requested issue exists in a candidate volume, and other information parsed from the filename.

The first result is a recommendation, not a guarantee. Relaunches, reprints, collected editions, foreign editions, and similarly named series can create legitimate ambiguity.

11. Filename Recommendations

For ordinary issues, a useful basic pattern is Series Issue (Year). Additional story-title text is fine as long as the important information remains recognizable.

  • Avengers 031 (2025).cbz
  • Batman 162 (2026).cbz
  • Aquaman 011 (2026).cbz
  • Action Comics 1080 (2025).cbz
  • Amazing Spider-Man - Torn 001 (2025).cbz

12. Request Limits and Background Enrichment

ComicVine limits how quickly applications can request information. Comic Zone schedules searches, previews, issue lookups, and metadata enrichment so it can retrieve the required information without unnecessarily exceeding that rate.

Interactive searches are prioritized. When you are waiting for the next picker search, it can take the next available request slot while lower-priority background enrichment waits. Background work resumes as capacity becomes available.

13. Troubleshooting

No useful results

Verify the series, issue or volume number, and year. Use Search Again and remove release-group names, scan tags, or other unnecessary filename text.

The wrong volume is ranked first

Compare the title, year, publisher, issue count, and cover. Use Show Issues before applying a questionable result.

The correct series is present but the issue is missing

Check another similarly named volume. ComicVine is community maintained, so entries may occasionally be incomplete or organized differently than expected.

A collected edition is confused with a single-issue series

Use the collection's volume number, year, title, cover, and Show Issues list together. The series name alone may not identify a trade or collection correctly.

14. Quick Workflow

Single comic:
Select Comic → Scrape → Start Scraping → Verify Result → Apply
Multiple comics:
Select Comics → Scrape → Start Scraping → Review When Needed → Apply or Skip → Continue
Uncertain match:
Select Candidate → Show Issues → Verify Cover / Number / Title → Apply
No correct result:
Search Again → Simplify Search → Verify Year / Number → Select Result → Apply

Tips for Best Results

  • Keep filenames reasonably clean and include an issue or volume number.
  • Include the year whenever possible.
  • Verify ambiguous volumes rather than relying only on the first result.
  • Use the cover preview as a visual cross-check.
  • Use Show Issues for relaunches, collections, and similarly named volumes.
  • Skip uncertain comics and return to them later rather than applying a questionable match.
